title: The Hasheesh Eater
summary: Background: Ludlow, the son of a prominent Abolitionist minister in New York, became best known through this book which chronicles his mind-altering experiences with cannabis alongside his philosophical ruminations while under the influence. The work is often compared to Thomas De Quincey's Confessions of an English Opium-Eater due to its detailed depiction of the author's opium addiction and his candid discussion of altered states of consciousness experienced with cannabis use.
